17:1.sourceText: Διοδεύσαντες δὲ τὴν Ἀμφίπολιν καὶ τὴν Ἀπολλωνίαν ἦλθον εἰς Θεσσαλονίκην, ὅπου ἦν συναγωγὴ τῶν Ἰουδαίων.
17:1.targetText: And having passed through Amphipolis, and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where the synagogue of the Jews was,

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles with the two place names have no separate English counterparts.

unmappedTarget.reason: The checked printed TR has an article before synagogue; the pinned N1904 synagogue noun is anarthrous.

17:2.sourceText: κατὰ δὲ τὸ εἰωθὸς τῷ Παύλῳ εἰσῆλθεν πρὸς αὐτοὺς, καὶ ἐπὶ σάββατα τρία διελέξατο αὐτοῖς ἀπὸ τῶν γραφῶν,
17:2.targetText: and according to the custom of Paul, he went in to them, and for three Sabbaths he was reasoning with them from the Writings,

groups.note: Actual εἰωθός is a substantival perfect active participle, the accustomed practice, rendered the noun custom.
The actual dative article and Paul jointly identify whose customary practice it was; English recasts this personal dative as of Paul.

Actual διελέξατο is aorist middle indicative third-person singular; the checked TR has imperfect διελέγετο behind the English was reasoning. The same reasoning predicate is retained with the actual tense stated.

17:3.sourceText: διανοίγων καὶ παρατιθέμενος ὅτι τὸν Χριστὸν ἔδει παθεῖν καὶ ἀναστῆναι ἐκ νεκρῶν, καὶ ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ Χριστός, ὁ Ἰησοῦς, ὃν ἐγὼ καταγγέλλω ὑμῖν.
17:3.targetText: opening and alleging that it was necessary [for] the Christ to suffer, and to rise again out of the dead, and that “this is the Christ—Jesus whom I proclaim to you.”

groups.note: The same source token παρατιθέμενος has functional middle and form passive analyses, V-PMP-NSM and V-PEP-NSM. It is rendered alleging; these are two analyses of one printed form.

Actual accusative article and Christ name supply the personal subject of the suffering infinitive under it was necessary; English makes this relation explicit with bracketed for. No separate Greek for preposition is asserted.
The substantival plural dead adjective is rendered the dead; its English article supports the nominal expression rather than supplying an additional printed Greek article.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article before the personal name Jesus has no separate English counterpart.

17:4.sourceText: καί τινες ἐξ αὐτῶν ἐπείσθησαν καὶ προσεκληρώθησαν τῷ Παύλῳ καὶ τῷ Σιλᾷ, τῶν τε σεβομένων Ἑλλήνων πλῆθος πολὺ, γυναικῶν τε τῶν πρώτων οὐκ ὀλίγαι.
17:4.targetText: And certain of them believed, and attached themselves to Paul and to Silas, also a great multitude of the worshiping Greeks, also not a few of the principal women.

groups.note: Actual ἐπείσθησαν is aorist passive, were persuaded, rendered believed; the source is πείθω, not a separately printed πιστεύω verb.
Actual προσεκληρώθησαν is aorist passive, were allotted or joined, rendered attached themselves. The English reflexive belongs to this predicate, not an independently printed Greek reflexive pronoun.

17:5.sourceText: Ζηλώσαντες δὲ οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ προσλαβόμενοι τῶν ἀγοραίων ἄνδρας τινὰς πονηροὺς καὶ ὀχλοποιήσαντες ἐθορύβουν τὴν πόλιν, καὶ ἐπιστάντες τῇ οἰκίᾳ Ἰάσονος ἐζήτουν αὐτοὺς προαγαγεῖν εἰς τὸν δῆμον·
17:5.targetText: And the Jews, having been moved with envy, and having taken to themselves certain evil men of the agitators, and having made a crowd, were setting the city in an uproar; having also assailed the house of Jason, they were seeking them to bring [them] to the populace,

groups.note: Actual ζηλώσαντες is an active aorist participle, having been jealous or envious; English uses the passive wording having been moved with envy for the same jealousy predicate.
Actual προσλαβόμενοι is a middle participle, taking to themselves; the English reflexive expresses this verb construction without a separate source pronoun.

Actual ἀγοραίων is a substantival marketplace adjective, here people of the marketplace, rendered agitators. This is the named translation’s contextual label for the marketplace people, not a separately printed Greek agitate verb. Primary dictionary: https://www.billmounce.com/greek-dictionary/agoraios .
The one actual αὐτούς names the people sought in order to bring them before the populace. English repeats that same immediate patient as them and bracketed them; only one source pronoun is written.

17:6.sourceText: μὴ εὑρόντες δὲ αὐτοὺς ἔσυρον Ἰάσονα καί τινας ἀδελφοὺς ἐπὶ τοὺς πολιτάρχας, βοῶντες ὅτι Οἱ τὴν οἰκουμένην ἀναστατώσαντες οὗτοι καὶ ἐνθάδε πάρεισιν,
17:6.targetText: and having not found them, they drew Jason and certain brothers to the city rulers, calling aloud, “These, having put the world in commotion, are also present here,

unmappedSource.reason: Greek ὅτι introduces the reported words; English quotation marks express the report without a separate that.
The Greek article introducing the world-disturbing participants has no separate English counterpart beside These.

17:7.sourceText: οὓς ὑποδέδεκται Ἰάσων· καὶ οὗτοι πάντες ἀπέναντι τῶν δογμάτων Καίσαρος πράσσουσιν, βασιλέα ἕτερον λέγοντες εἶναι Ἰησοῦν.
17:7.targetText: whom Jason has received; and all these do contrary to the decrees of Caesar, saying another to be king—Jesus.”

17:8.sourceText: ἐτάραξαν δὲ τὸν ὄχλον καὶ τοὺς πολιτάρχας ἀκούοντας ταῦτα,
17:8.targetText: And they troubled the multitude and the city rulers, hearing these things,

17:9.sourceText: καὶ λαβόντες τὸ ἱκανὸν παρὰ τοῦ Ἰάσονος καὶ τῶν λοιπῶν ἀπέλυσαν αὐτούς.
17:9.targetText: and having taken security from Jason and the rest, they let them go.

groups.note: Actual article plus substantival sufficient adjective forms the security or sufficient guarantee expression. English security names this whole nominal construction, not an independently printed Greek security noun.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article with Jason has no separate English counterpart.

17:10.sourceText: Οἱ δὲ ἀδελφοὶ εὐθέως διὰ νυκτὸς ἐξέπεμψαν τόν τε Παῦλον καὶ τὸν Σιλᾶν εἰς Βέροιαν, οἵτινες παραγενόμενοι εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἀπῄεσαν·
17:10.targetText: And the brothers immediately, through the night, sent forth both Paul and Silas to Berea, who having come, went into the synagogue of the Jews;

groups.note: Actual night is anarthrous in N1904; the checked TR has an article with night. English the night is the same temporal noun phrase; no additional original article is invented.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles with Paul and Silas have no separate English counterparts.

17:11.sourceText: οὗτοι δὲ ἦσαν εὐγενέστεροι τῶν ἐν Θεσσαλονίκῃ, οἵτινες ἐδέξαντο τὸν λόγον μετὰ πάσης προθυμίας, τὸ καθ’ ἡμέραν ἀνακρίνοντες τὰς γραφὰς εἰ ἔχοι ταῦτα οὕτως.
17:11.targetText: and these were more noble than those in Thessalonica; they received the word with all readiness of mind, examining the Writings every day [to see] whether those things were so;

groups.note: The actual genitive article substantivizes the people in Thessalonica and marks the comparison after more noble; English renders the case-bearing participant expression than those.
Actual οἵτινες is a relative participant, who; English starts a fresh clause with the same people as they.

Actual ἔχοι is present active optative third-person singular in the whether clause, literally how the things might stand; English uses were so. The original is ἔχω with an optative analysis, not a printed εἰμί copula.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article introduces the distributive daily expression; English every day does not give it a separate counterpart.

unmappedTarget.reason: This bracketed purpose wording is supplied in English; no seeing verb is written in either the pinned N1904 or the checked TR.

17:12.sourceText: πολλοὶ μὲν οὖν ἐξ αὐτῶν ἐπίστευσαν, καὶ τῶν Ἑλληνίδων γυναικῶν τῶν εὐσχημόνων καὶ ἀνδρῶν οὐκ ὀλίγοι.
17:12.targetText: therefore, many of them, indeed, believed, and not a few of the honorable Greek women and men.

groups.note: Actual Ἑλληνίδων is the feminine ethnic designation, recorded N-GPF in both pinned analyses. English uses Greek as a modifier of women; no source adjective tag is substituted for the recorded noun analysis.

unmappedSource.reason: The second Greek article attributively marks the honorable women; English has only the one article already represented in of the.

17:13.sourceText: Ὡς δὲ ἔγνωσαν οἱ ἀπὸ τῆς Θεσσαλονίκης Ἰουδαῖοι ὅτι καὶ ἐν τῇ Βεροίᾳ κατηγγέλη ὑπὸ τοῦ Παύλου ὁ λόγος τοῦ Θεοῦ, ἦλθον κἀκεῖ σαλεύοντες καὶ ταράσσοντες τοὺς ὄχλους.
17:13.targetText: And when the Jews from Thessalonica knew that also in Berea was the word of God declared by Paul, they came there also, agitating the multitudes;

groups.note: Actual κἀκεῖ is a crasis of and with there; English gives its additive force as there also. Both English pieces belong to this one actual adverb.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles with Thessalonica, Berea, and Paul have no separate English counterparts.
N1904 additionally writes and troubling after agitating. This second coordinated predicate is absent from the checked printed TR and has no separate English counterpart.

17:14.sourceText: εὐθέως δὲ τότε τὸν Παῦλον ἐξαπέστειλαν οἱ ἀδελφοὶ πορεύεσθαι ἕως ἐπὶ τὴν θάλασσαν· ὑπέμεινάν τε ὅ τε Σιλᾶς καὶ ὁ Τιμόθεος ἐκεῖ.
17:14.targetText: and then immediately the brothers sent forth Paul, to go on as it were to the sea, but both Silas and Timotheus were remaining there.

groups.note: Actual ὑπέμειναν is aorist active indicative third-person plural; checked TR ὑπέμενον is imperfect behind were remaining. The actual remaining predicate is retained without assigning it the TR tense.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles with the three personal names have no separate English counterparts.
Actual ἕως marks the extent, as far as; the checked TR instead has ὡς, behind as it were. These different printed forms are not treated as one original identity.
Actual τε is additive coordination here; checked TR instead has δέ before the remaining companions, rendered but.

unmappedTarget.reason: This follows checked TR ὡς, whereas the pinned N1904 has ἕως, as far as.
This follows the checked TR δέ connective; N1904 writes additive τε at that point.

17:15.sourceText: οἱ δὲ καθιστάνοντες τὸν Παῦλον ἤγαγον ἕως Ἀθηνῶν, καὶ λαβόντες ἐντολὴν πρὸς τὸν Σιλᾶν καὶ τὸν Τιμόθεον ἵνα ὡς τάχιστα ἔλθωσιν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἐξῄεσαν.
17:15.targetText: And those conducting Paul, brought him to Athens, and having received a command to Silas and Timotheus that with all speed they may come to him, they departed;

groups.note: Actual καθιστάνοντες is a present active conducting or escorting participle; this is the escort sense of καθίστημι, not an appointment to office. Primary dictionary: https://www.billmounce.com/greek-dictionary/kathistemi .

The one actual Paul name supplies the immediately conducted and brought patient; English resumes him after the same conducting-Paul phrase. N1904 has no second object pronoun here, whereas the checked TR prints αὐτόν after brought. No autos identity is invented in N1904.

Actual ὡς with the superlative adverb τάχιστα forms as quickly as possible, rendered with all speed. The whole speed construction is retained without inventing separate Greek with, all, or speed-noun words.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles with Paul, Silas, and Timothy have no separate English counterparts.

17:16.sourceText: Ἐν δὲ ταῖς Ἀθήναις ἐκδεχομένου αὐτοὺς τοῦ Παύλου, παρωξύνετο τὸ πνεῦμα αὐτοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ θεωροῦντος κατείδωλον οὖσαν τὴν πόλιν.
17:16.targetText: and Paul waiting for them in Athens, his spirit was stirred in him, beholding the city wholly given to idolatry,

groups.note: Actual παρωξύνετο is imperfect passive functionally, V-IPI-3S, with form analysis V-IEI-3S. These are two analyses of the one printed stirred form, rendered was stirred.

Actual θεωροῦντος is genitive singular and shares the genitive Paul as beholding participant. The checked TR uses dative θεωροῦντι; the same beholding predicate is retained with its actual genitive analysis.
Actual κατείδωλον is one compound adjective, idol-filled, rendered wholly given to idolatry. No independent Greek giving verb or idolatry noun is printed in this phrase.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles with Athens, Paul, and his spirit have no separate English counterparts.
The Greek being participle makes the city’s idol-filled property explicit; English directly attaches wholly given to idolatry to city without separately expressing being.

17:17.sourceText: διελέγετο μὲν οὖν ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις καὶ τοῖς σεβομένοις καὶ ἐν τῇ ἀγορᾷ κατὰ πᾶσαν ἡμέραν πρὸς τοὺς παρατυγχάνοντας.
17:17.targetText: therefore, indeed, he was reasoning in the synagogue with the Jews, and with the worshiping persons, and in the marketplace every day with those who met with him.

groups.note: Actual worshiping is a substantival participle, rendered worshiping persons; persons supplies English nominal support without an additional printed Greek person noun.
Actual κατά with every forms the distributive every-day relation; English every expresses the paired distributive construction, not a separate Greek every preposition.

unmappedTarget.reason: The encounter participle has no independently written personal object here in either N1904 or the checked TR. English supplies the person encountered from the surrounding Paul narrative; no cross-verse person anchor is synthesized.

17:18.sourceText: τινὲς δὲ καὶ τῶν Ἐπικουρίων καὶ Στοϊκῶν φιλοσόφων συνέβαλλον αὐτῷ, καί τινες ἔλεγον Τί ἂν θέλοι ὁ σπερμολόγος οὗτος λέγειν; οἱ δέ· Ξένων δαιμονίων δοκεῖ καταγγελεὺς εἶναι· ὅτι τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ τὴν ἀνάστασιν εὐηγγελίζετο.
17:18.targetText: And certain of the Epicurean and of the Stoic philosophers, were meeting together to see him, and some were saying, “What would this seed picker wish to say?” And others, “He seems to be an announcer of strange demons”; because he proclaimed to them Jesus and the resurrection as good news,

groups.note: The one actual genitive article governs the coordinated Epicurean and Stoic philosopher expression. English repeats of the across the coordinated modifiers; this retains one original article identity, not a second printed article.
Actual Ἐπικουρίων is recorded N-GPM in both pinned analyses; English uses Epicurean as a modifier of philosophers. Its recorded noun analysis is retained.

Actual συμβάλλω expresses meeting or encountering, here rendered were meeting together to see. To see expands this English encounter expression; there is no separately printed seeing verb. Actual αὐτῷ is the dative encounter participant, rendered him under that English construction.
The potential particle and optative wishing verb jointly supply would wish; the actual verb is present active optative third-person singular.

Actual σπερμολόγος is a substantival compound adjective, literally seed-picking, rendered seed picker. It is one original word, not separate seed and picking words. Primary dictionary: https://www.billmounce.com/greek-dictionary/spermologos .

Actual εὐηγγελίζετο is one proclaiming-good-news verb, with functional middle and form passive analyses, V-IMI-3S/V-IEI-3S. English splits its predicate around the announced objects as he proclaimed and as good news; no independent good/news nouns are printed.

unmappedSource.reason: The initial additional also particle is not separately expressed in English.
The Greek articles with this seed-picker and the personal name Jesus have no separate English counterparts.

unmappedTarget.reason: The checked TR has an additional αὐτοῖς recipient pronoun in the proclamation clause; N1904 has no such written recipient here.

17:19.sourceText: ἐπιλαβόμενοί δὲ αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸν Ἄρειον πάγον ἤγαγον, λέγοντες Δυνάμεθα γνῶναι τίς ἡ καινὴ αὕτη ἡ ὑπὸ σοῦ λαλουμένη διδαχή;
17:19.targetText: having also taken him, they brought [him] to the Areopagus, saying, “Are we able to know what this new teaching [is] that is spoken by you,

groups.note: Actual genitive αὐτοῦ is the taken participant and immediately also the brought participant. English repeats him for those two coordinated actions; one real genitive source pronoun is retained, not a new accusative autos word.
Actual Ἄρειον Πάγον is a two-word place name, jointly rendered Areopagus. Both actual name words retain their own identity within the shared English name.

Actual λαλουμένη is the passive speaking participle rendered is spoken; the English auxiliary belongs to this real verbal participle. Its functional V-PPP-NSF and form V-PEP-NSF analyses are two tags of the same source token.

unmappedSource.reason: The first Greek article with this new teaching has no separate English counterpart beside this.

unmappedTarget.reason: The bracketed copula in what this new teaching is is supplied in English; neither N1904 nor the checked TR writes an independent being word in that question.

17:20.sourceText: ξενίζοντα γάρ τινα εἰσφέρεις εἰς τὰς ἀκοὰς ἡμῶν· βουλόμεθα οὖν γνῶναι τίνα θέλει ταῦτα εἶναι.
17:20.targetText: for you bring certain strange things to our ears? We resolve, then, to know what these things would wish to be”;

groups.note: Actual ξενίζοντα is a substantival active participle, things that strike as strange; English renders the property nominally as strange things.

Actual θέλει is present active indicative third-person singular, with the neuter plural these things as subject; checked TR θέλοι is optative behind would wish. The same wishing or meaning predicate is retained without assigning the source an optative tag.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article with our ears has no separate English counterpart with the possessive.

17:21.sourceText: Ἀθηναῖοι δὲ πάντες καὶ οἱ ἐπιδημοῦντες ξένοι εἰς οὐδὲν ἕτερον ηὐκαίρουν ἢ λέγειν τι ἢ ἀκούειν τι καινότερον.
17:21.targetText: and all Athenians, and the strangers sojourning, for nothing else were at leisure but to say something, and to hear some newer thing.

groups.note: Actual Athenians is a substantival ethnic adjective, recorded A-NPM in both pinned analyses; English gives the same people designation as Athenians.
Actual καινότερον is comparative, newer, used substantivally; thing is English nominal support for that adjective, not a separately printed Greek thing noun.

unmappedSource.reason: Actual ἤ is or between saying and hearing; the checked TR has καί behind the English and. These distinct coordination words are not merged into one identity.

unmappedTarget.reason: This follows the checked TR καί between saying and hearing; N1904 instead writes ἤ, or.

17:22.sourceText: Σταθεὶς δὲ Παῦλος ἐν μέσῳ τοῦ Ἀρείου Πάγου ἔφη Ἄνδρες Ἀθηναῖοι, κατὰ πάντα ὡς δεισιδαιμονεστέρους ὑμᾶς θεωρῶ.
17:22.targetText: And Paul, having stood in the midst of the Areopagus, said, “Men, Athenians, in all things I perceive you as over-religious;

groups.note: Actual σταθείς is an aorist passive-form standing participle, rendered having stood; the actual passive morphology is retained without adding an external standing agent.
The actual genitive article and two-word Areopagus name jointly supply of the Areopagus. No bare English of is assigned to the article apart from its nominal head.

Actual δεισιδαιμονεστέρους is a comparative religious adjective, rendered over-religious. This records the source form and the named translation’s wording. Primary dictionary: https://www.billmounce.com/greek-dictionary/deisidaimon .

17:23.sourceText: διερχόμενος γὰρ καὶ ἀναθεωρῶν τὰ σεβάσματα ὑμῶν εὗρον καὶ βωμὸν ἐν ᾧ ἐπεγέγραπτο ΑΓΝΩΣΤΩ ΘΕΩ. ὃ οὖν ἀγνοοῦντες εὐσεβεῖτε, τοῦτο ἐγὼ καταγγέλλω ὑμῖν.
17:23.targetText: for passing through and contemplating your objects of worship, I also found an altar on which had been inscribed: To God—unknown; whom, therefore—not knowing—you worship, this One I announce to you.

groups.note: Actual σεβάσματα is one plural worship-object noun, rendered objects of worship; no independent source object and worship words are manufactured.
Actual God is dative in the altar inscription, jointly expressing the English dedicatory To God. No independently printed Greek to preposition is asserted.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article with your objects of worship has no separate English counterpart beside the possessive.

Actual ὃ is a neuter relative, what or that which, whereas the checked TR has masculine ὅν behind English whom. The source pronoun’s actual gender and written identity are retained as an explained witness difference.
Actual τοῦτο is neuter this, whereas checked TR τοῦτον is masculine behind English this One. These differently printed demonstrative forms are not treated as the same source occurrence.

unmappedTarget.reason: English follows the checked TR masculine relative ὅν; N1904 instead has neuter ὃ.
English follows the checked TR masculine τοῦτον; N1904 instead has neuter τοῦτο.

17:24.sourceText: ὁ Θεὸς ὁ ποιήσας τὸν κόσμον καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐν αὐτῷ, οὗτος οὐρανοῦ καὶ γῆς ὑπάρχων Κύριος οὐκ ἐν χειροποιήτοις ναοῖς κατοικεῖ,
17:24.targetText: God, who made the world, and all things in it, this One, being Lord of Heaven and of earth, does not dwell in temples made with hands,

groups.note: Actual χειροποιήτοις is one hand-made adjective, rendered made with hands. It does not supply independently printed making, with, and hands words.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article before God has no separate English counterpart.
The second Greek article after all introduces the things in the world; English all things in it has no separately expressed second article.

17:25.sourceText: οὐδὲ ὑπὸ χειρῶν ἀνθρωπίνων θεραπεύεται προσδεόμενός τινος, αὐτὸς διδοὺς πᾶσι ζωὴν καὶ πνοὴν καὶ τὰ πάντα·
17:25.targetText: neither is He served by the hands of men—needing anything, He giving life to all, and breath, and all things;

groups.note: Actual θεραπεύεται is present passive functionally, V-PPI-3S, with form V-PEI-3S, rendered is He served. These are two analyses of one token, not two written forms.

Actual ἀνθρωπίνων is a genitive human adjective, recorded A-GPF in both analyses, rendered of men. The checked TR instead prints the men noun ἀνθρώπων. The actual human modifier is retained without replacing it by the TR noun annotation.

17:26.sourceText: ἐποίησέν τε ἐξ ἑνὸς πᾶν ἔθνος ἀνθρώπων κατοικεῖν ἐπὶ παντὸς προσώπου τῆς γῆς, ὁρίσας προστεταγμένους καιροὺς καὶ τὰς ὁροθεσίας τῆς κατοικίας αὐτῶν,
17:26.targetText: He also made every nation of man of one blood, to dwell on all the face of the earth—having ordained times before appointed, and the bounds of their dwellings—

groups.note: Actual ἀνθρώπων is genitive plural humans; English of man uses a collective singular expression for that same human population.

Actual προστεταγμένους is a perfect passive participle from προστάσσω, ordered or appointed; checked TR προτεταγμένους has the different prior-appointment prefix. Only the shared appointment predicate is linked; English before is separately explained.

The actual genitive article and dwelling noun jointly supply of ... dwellings, with their retaining the distinct real possessive pronoun. The source noun is singular dwelling, while English uses plural dwellings.

unmappedTarget.reason: The checked TR writes an additional blood noun after one; N1904 writes of one without that noun.
The checked TR has an article with face; the pinned N1904 genitive face phrase is anarthrous.

Checked TR προτεταγμένους is the appointed-before compound behind before appointed; N1904 instead writes προστεταγμένους, from προστάσσω, order or appoint. No separate anterior-time word is invented in that source token.

17:27.sourceText: ζητεῖν τὸν Θεὸν, εἰ ἄρα γε ψηλαφήσειαν αὐτὸν καὶ εὕροιεν, καί γε οὐ μακρὰν ἀπὸ ἑνὸς ἑκάστου ἡμῶν ὑπάρχοντα.
17:27.targetText: to seek the LORD, if perhaps they felt after Him and found, though, indeed, He is not far from each one of us,

groups.note: Actual ψηλαφήσειαν is aorist active optative third-person plural in the if-perhaps frame; English felt after uses past-tense wording while retaining the actual groping or feeling predicate.
Actual εὕροιεν is second-aorist active optative third-person plural in the same hypothetical frame; English found does not retag it as indicative.
Actual καί with the following emphatic γε introduces the contrast, rendered though indeed. N1904 writes these as separate words rather than the checked TR καίτοιγε compound.

Actual ὑπάρχοντα is an accusative present active participle in the same God-seeking sentence; English recasts its existing/not-far property as the finite He is not far clause. No independent Greek He pronoun or finite copula is printed here.

unmappedSource.reason: The pinned source article and God name differ from the checked TR article and LORD name followed by the English the LORD. No LORD lemma is borrowed from the other printed witness.
The first Greek γε emphasizes perhaps; English has no separate emphasis counterpart at this first location. The later actual γε owns indeed.

unmappedTarget.reason: The checked TR writes τὸν κύριον here, whereas N1904 writes τὸν Θεόν.

17:28.sourceText: ἐν αὐτῷ γὰρ ζῶμεν καὶ κινούμεθα καὶ ἐσμέν, ὡς καί τινες τῶν καθ’ ὑμᾶς ποιητῶν εἰρήκασιν Τοῦ γὰρ καὶ γένος ἐσμέν.
17:28.targetText: for in Him we live, and move, and are; as certain of your poets have also said: For we are also His offspring.

groups.note: Actual κινούμεθα has functional passive and form passive analyses, V-PPI-1P/V-PEI-1P, while English uses move in an active intransitive expression. The real moving predicate and its recorded source analyses remain visible.
The actual genitive article and poets noun jointly supply the of ... poets complement; your retains the distinct actual among-you construction.

Actual καθ᾽ ὑμᾶς specifies the poets among or belonging with you; English recasts this prepositional personal association as possessive your. The source pronoun is accusative, not an independently printed genitive possessive.
Actual Τοῦ is the genitive article used pronominally in the quoted wording, of him, rendered His. Its recorded article identity is retained; no αὐτοῦ pronoun is substituted.

17:29.sourceText: γένος οὖν ὑπάρχοντες τοῦ Θεοῦ οὐκ ὀφείλομεν νομίζειν, χρυσῷ ἢ ἀργύρῳ ἢ λίθῳ, χαράγματι τέχνης καὶ ἐνθυμήσεως ἀνθρώπου, τὸ Θεῖον εἶναι ὅμοιον.
17:29.targetText: Being, therefore, offspring of God, we ought not to think the Godhead to be like to gold, or silver, or stone, [an] engraving of art and imagination of man;

groups.note: Actual genitive article and God name jointly supply of God; the relational English of stays with its actual nominal head.
Actual Θεῖον is a substantival neuter divine adjective, rendered Godhead. The English noun expresses that original nominal adjective rather than a separately printed Godhead noun.
Actual χαράγματι is dative, in apposition with the material likeness expression; English gives an engraving as the appositional noun. Bracketed an is English indefinite nominal support.

17:30.sourceText: τοὺς μὲν οὖν χρόνους τῆς ἀγνοίας ὑπεριδὼν ὁ Θεὸς τὰ νῦν ἀπαγγέλλει τοῖς ἀνθρώποις πάντας πανταχοῦ μετανοεῖν,
17:30.targetText: therefore indeed God, having overlooked the times of ignorance, now commands all men everywhere to convert,

groups.note: The actual genitive article and ignorance noun jointly supply of ignorance; the bare relation is kept with the real nominal head.
Actual τὰ νῦν is the article-plus-now adverbial expression, rendered now. Both actual words are retained in this one temporal construction.

Actual πάντας is accusative plural within the repentance infinitive frame, while men is the preceding dative ἀνθρώποις. English all men recasts these same people as the command recipients and understood repentance subjects; the actual differing case analyses are retained.
Actual μετανοεῖν is the present active repenting or changing-mind infinitive, rendered to convert. The actual μετάνοια-family verb is retained, not a separately printed turning verb.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article before God has no separate English counterpart.
The Greek article with men has no separate English counterpart under all men.

Actual ἀπαγγέλλει is the announcing or reporting verb, while the checked TR has the different commanding verb παραγγέλλει behind English commands. The different compound heads are not collapsed into a guessed lexical link.

unmappedTarget.reason: This follows the checked TR παραγγέλλει; N1904 instead writes ἀπαγγέλλει, announces or reports.

17:31.sourceText: καθότι ἔστησεν ἡμέραν ἐν ᾗ μέλλει κρίνειν τὴν οἰκουμένην ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ, ἐν ἀνδρὶ ᾧ ὥρισεν, πίστιν παρασχὼν πᾶσιν ἀναστήσας αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν.
17:31.targetText: because He set a day in which He is about to judge the world in righteousness, by a Man whom He ordained, having given assurance to all, having raised Him out of the dead.”

groups.note: Actual ᾧ is the dative relative associated with the preceding dative man; English renders the appointed participant as whom. The real dative relative form is retained rather than retagging it accusative from the English wording.
Actual πίστιν is the faith, trust, or assurance noun, here rendered assurance in the giving construction; no independent Greek assurance verb is supplied.
Actual πᾶσιν is a substantival dative all, rendered to all; the English to expresses this actual dative recipient relation, not an unwritten source preposition.

17:32.sourceText: ἀκούσαντες δὲ ἀνάστασιν νεκρῶν, οἱ μὲν ἐχλεύαζον, οἱ δὲ εἶπαν Ἀκουσόμεθά σου περὶ τούτου καὶ πάλιν.
17:32.targetText: And having heard of a resurrection of the dead, some, indeed, were mocking, but others said, “We will hear you again concerning this”;

groups.note: Actual νεκρῶν is a genitive plural dead adjective used substantivally, rendered of the dead. The whole case-bearing nominal expression supplies the English relation and article support.
Actual οἱ is a substantival plural article in the contrasted participant pair, rendered some; the later article separately owns others.

unmappedSource.reason: N1904 writes an additional καί, also, before again; the checked TR and this English wording have no separately expressed additive at that point.

17:33.sourceText: οὕτως ὁ Παῦλος ἐξῆλθεν ἐκ μέσου αὐτῶν.
17:33.targetText: and so Paul went forth from the midst of them,

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article with Paul has no separate English counterpart.

unmappedTarget.reason: The checked TR has an additional initial καί before so; it is absent from the pinned N1904 verse.

17:34.sourceText: τινὲς δὲ ἄνδρες κολληθέντες αὐτῷ ἐπίστευσαν, ἐν οἷς καὶ Διονύσιος ὁ Ἀρεοπαγείτης καὶ γυνὴ ὀνόματι Δάμαρις καὶ ἕτεροι σὺν αὐτοῖς.
17:34.targetText: and certain men having cleaved to him, believed, among whom [is] also Dionysius the Areopagite, and a woman, by name Damaris, and others with them.

groups.note: Actual κολληθέντες is an aorist passive participle, were joined or attached; English uses having cleaved. The actual passive morphology is retained, without inventing a separate reflexive pronoun.
Actual ὀνόματι is a dative name noun, rendered by name; the English by expresses the nominal case construction rather than an additional printed Greek preposition.

unmappedTarget.reason: The bracketed is after among whom is supplied for the English list; neither N1904 nor the checked TR writes an independent copula there.
